lines.text: Tobin's grandfather was a smith in Greyhollow, back when nobody in Greyhollow owned anything worth hitting with a hammer.
His forge-book was mostly horseshoes. But on the last page he had drawn a sword, half steel and half clear glass, with a note so cramped that Tobin had been squinting at it since summer.
Steel folded with rimeglass, my lord. Forty folds, quenched in snowmelt from the Pale. He says it cuts what isn't there.
What isn't there?
Aether, I think. He never made one. Nobody could afford the glass, in his day. Except you. Beast glass only, my lord. I know the law.
So the forge burned for nine days. Tobin didn't sleep. Neither did the six apprentices he'd borrowed, though nobody had asked them.
The first blade shattered on the anvil. The second one melted. The third one exploded, and took both of Tobin's eyebrows with it.
He said it didn't matter. He was bald already. There was nothing left up there to lose.
The fortieth blade came out of the snowmelt grey, with an edge as clear as river ice. Tobin held it up to the light, and for once said nothing.
We tested it in the yard. Oswin wrapped his sword in frost, four rings of Rime, hard as iron.
Go on, then, Sir Tobin. Hit it. If it breaks, you owe me a sword.
Tobin swung. The glass-steel went through Oswin's frost as if it were mist, and stopped a hair from the steel underneath.
I felt that in my teeth. It didn't cut the sword, my lord. It cut the frost off it.
Then Ilse brought out Penhallow's ring. Milky blue glass, with the Order's mark inside. Seven rings around an eye.
Borrowed aether. Everything a bought lord has, he keeps in here. Touch it with the edge, Tobin.
The edge touched the ring. The light inside went out, like a candle pinched between two fingers, and the glass went grey and dead.
It's cold now. Somebody was in it.
Nobody said anything after that. Ilse wrapped the dead ring in a cloth, very gently, as if it might still be someone.
We buried it that night, beside Dunn. It seemed the decent thing to do.
A blade that cuts what isn't there. Every bought ring in the royal army. Every lord who had borrowed his power from a child in a cellar. Tobin had made a knife for all of them.
Forty blades by the new moon, my lord. If I don't sleep.
And how many do we need?
All of them, my lord. The beacon line's nearly finished, and the King's army is moving again.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter one hundred and twenty-four, coming soon.
